Clean author names by Scopus author ID

Source: R/authors_clean.R
authors_clean.Rd

Gives each person one spelling in the author column of a bibliometrix data frame, and returns the data frame ready for bibliometrix.

* `level = "confirmed"` (default): all spellings of one Scopus author ID become one. Nothing else is used, and no network is needed. * `level = "needs_decision"`: the confirmed merges, plus the merges you accepted in a decisions sheet. The first run asks OpenAlex, by DOI, for each author's ORCID and writes the Scopus IDs that share one ORCID to `decisions`; nothing from it is applied yet. Write `merge` in its `decision` column for the right ones and run again: the sheet is then read, without asking OpenAlex.

A person's spelling is the one used most often in `data`, then the most recent, then the longest. Authors who were not merged keep their spelling, and a paper with no merged author is left as it was. Different Scopus IDs that share a spelling stay as they are: they are not numbered or split.

The Scopus author IDs are matched to the papers by record ID (the Scopus EID, ignoring case: bibliometrix writes `2-S2.0-...`, Scopus `2-s2.0-...`), then by position: the *i*-th author of a paper takes its *i*-th ID. A paper whose record is not in `ids`, or whose number of authors and of IDs differ, is left untouched; the message names the reasons.

Usage

authors_clean(
  data,
  ids,
  record_id = "eid",
  authors = "AU",
  full_names = "AF",
  year = "PY",
  level = c("confirmed", "needs_decision"),
  decisions = NULL,
  doi = "DI",
  mailto = NULL,
  output = c("minimal", "all")
)

Arguments

data

A bibliometrix data frame, one row per paper. The result of another cleaner works too: `M |> authors_clean(ids = "scopus_exports") |> keywords_clean()`.

ids

The Scopus author IDs: paths to raw Scopus CSV exports, a folder holding them, or a data frame. Each needs the columns `EID` and `Author(s) ID`; `Authors` is used, when present, to match names on OpenAlex. bibliometrix drops the IDs, so they must be given here.

record_id

Name of the column in `data` holding the Scopus EID (`"2-s2.0-..."`). Default `"eid"`.

authors

Name of the author column (`;`-separated). Default `"AU"`.

full_names

Name of the full-name column, rewritten alongside `authors` on papers where it has as many names. Default `"AF"`, skipped when `data` has no such column; `NULL` leaves it alone.

year

Name of the publication-year column, used to break ties between spellings. Default `"PY"`, skipped when absent.

level

`"confirmed"` (default) or `"needs_decision"`; see above.

decisions

With `level = "needs_decision"`: the decisions sheet, a path ending in `.csv` or `.xlsx`. Written when it does not exist, read when it does.

doi

Name of the DOI column, used to ask OpenAlex. Default `"DI"`.

mailto

Optional e-mail address sent to OpenAlex to use its polite pool. Default `NULL` sends none.

output

`"minimal"` (default) returns `data` with `authors` and `full_names` rewritten and nothing added. `"all"` also adds `AU_ORIGINAL` (and `AF_ORIGINAL`), the columns as they came in (kept, not replaced, when `data` already has them); `AU_ID`, the Scopus IDs in the order of the authors (`NA` for an untouched paper); and `check_authors`, `"YES"` for a paper with an author whose merged spellings do not look like one name (`"ENDRASS B"` and `"LUGRIN B"` under one Scopus ID), else `"NO"`.

Value

`data`, same class, rows and columns, with the author column (and the full-name column) rewritten; with `output = "all"`, plus the columns described under `output`. A message reports the counts, and why any paper was left untouched.

Errors

Raises `saqrmisc_bad_input` when `data` lacks a named column or repeats a record ID, `ids` names no readable export or lacks `EID` / `Author(s) ID`, no record of `data` is in `ids`, `decisions` is given with `level = "confirmed"` or missing with `"needs_decision"`, or the decisions sheet lacks `scopus_ids` / `decision` or holds a decision other than empty, `merge` or `no`; `saqrmisc_missing_package` when OpenAlex is needed without httr2, or for an `.xlsx` sheet without writexl / readxl. Warns `saqrmisc_review_unmatched` for decided Scopus IDs not in `data`, and `saqrmisc_openalex_failed` for failed OpenAlex requests.

References

Baas, J., Schotten, M., Plume, A., Côté, G., & Karimi, R. (2020). Scopus as a curated, high-quality bibliometric data source for academic research in quantitative science studies. *Quantitative Science Studies*, 1(1), 377-386. doi:10.1162/qss_a_00019

Priem, J., Piwowar, H., & Orr, R. (2022). OpenAlex: A fully-open index of scholarly works, authors, venues, institutions, and concepts. arXiv:2205.01833.

Examples

scopus <- data.frame(
  EID = c("2-s2.0-1", "2-s2.0-2", "2-s2.0-3"),
  `Author(s) ID` = c("111;201;", "111;202;", "111;"),
  check.names = FALSE
)
M <- data.frame(
  eid = c("2-s2.0-1", "2-s2.0-2", "2-s2.0-3"),
  AU = c("PREZ-MARN D;KIM J", "PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J", "PEREZ-MARIN D"),
  PY = c(2019, 2020, 2021)
)
authors_clean(M, ids = scopus)
#> authors_clean: 1 people given one spelling (0 by decision); 1 papers changed; 0 papers to check; 0 papers untouched
#>        eid                  AU   PY
#> 1 2-s2.0-1 PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J 2019
#> 2 2-s2.0-2 PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J 2020
#> 3 2-s2.0-3       PEREZ-MARIN D 2021
authors_clean(M, ids = scopus, output = "all")
#> authors_clean: 1 people given one spelling (0 by decision); 1 papers changed; 0 papers to check; 0 papers untouched
#>        eid                  AU   PY         AU_ORIGINAL   AU_ID check_authors
#> 1 2-s2.0-1 PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J 2019   PREZ-MARN D;KIM J 111;201            NO
#> 2 2-s2.0-2 PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J 2020 PEREZ-MARIN D;KIM J 111;202            NO
#> 3 2-s2.0-3       PEREZ-MARIN D 2021       PEREZ-MARIN D     111            NO
